title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Media Availability | Friday, September 25th | Press Conference
headline: Michael Penix Jr. is confirmed as the starting QB for the Monday night game after the Falcons' first win. The run game was effective, Drake London got 10 targets to Kyle Pitts' 2, and Stefanski insists Pitts will be a big part of the offense.
summary: Stefanski was happy with the win, praising the effort, the physicality and the way the offense, defense and special teams fed off each other. He said the offense was cleaner because everyone was on the same page, with the run game, tight ends and receivers all involved and Penix handling pre-snap communication well. He did not read Penix's slow start, including an early interception, as pressing. He said the quarterback settled in and took advantage of the looks he was given, and he credited the offensive coordinator, Tommy, for mixing run and pass. He confirmed Penix as the starter for next week. The defense got consistent pressure from its front, and Stefanski singled out Gervon Dexter for his size, length and ability to push the pocket. He praised Billy Bowman for his energy in his return from injury, Nick Muse for his special teams tackles, and Kendal Daniels for diagnosing screens. On the Pitts versus London target split, he said the ball goes where the defense allows and that the game plan doesn't change. Harold Perkins played a high share of snaps, but Stefanski said snap counts will depend on the opponent's personnel. The team is off for a few days, then works Monday and Tuesday, has Wednesday off, and starts its week for the Monday night game on Thursday.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Post-game Press Conference | Week 3 | Falcons vs Packers
headline: Penix returned from injury and looked solid in a balanced offense. Bijan Robinson, Brian Robinson and Drake London (9 catches, 194 yards) all got strong praise after the win over Green Bay.
summary: Stefanski was proud of the team's effort on a short week and highlighted complementary football: special teams covered kicks well, the defense got a third-quarter stop, and the offense answered with a 90-yard touchdown drive. He said Michael Penix Jr. was playing his first game back from injury, so some rust was expected, but he battled, made good decisions and had mostly good protection. Tommy (the play-caller) leaned on concepts Penix is comfortable with and spread the ball around, including early screens, which Stefanski framed as taking what the defense gave. He called the run game outstanding, crediting the line, tight ends and receivers for blocking, and said both Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson were excellent. He praised Bijan's unique running style and leadership, and called Drake London a huge part of the offense, saying the team needs to spread the ball around to be balanced. The defense harassed Jordan Love and held Green Bay to under 20 rushing yards, and Stefanski said pressure matters more than sack totals. He also pointed to the field-goal block unit as a strength, with big bodies like Gervon Dexter and Maason Smith. He avoided talk of statements or momentum, stressing turnover margin and taking each week as it comes.

injuries.detail: Played his first game after injury rehab. Stefanski cited jitters and rust but praised his battle, decision-making and the extra work he put in.

signals.claim: Penix is back playing quarterback after injury and ran an offense built on concepts he's comfortable with.
signals.note: Stefanski is encouraged by Penix's decision-making and says the performance is something to build on, which supports his QB outlook.
signals.quote: Mike made great decisions with the ball.

signals.claim: Bijan remains a central piece of the offense and the run game.
signals.note: Stefanski called him a team leader the team is counting on, and the run game was a strength.

signals.quote: I thought Bijan and Brian were both outstanding.

signals.note: After a 9-catch, 194-yard game, Stefanski called him a huge part of the offense and said Penix made the right reads to him.

topics.detail: Tommy spread the ball to many players and used screens early, which Stefanski described as taking what the defense allowed. The run game worked because of blocking from receivers, tight ends and the offensive line.
The defense limited Green Bay's rushing to under 20 yards and pressured Jordan Love often. Stefanski said sacks can be misleading and that pressure was the goal.
Kick coverage was strong and the field-goal block unit made a play. Stefanski noted that Zach (likely Zach Harrison), Gervon Dexter and Maason Smith give them size for blocking kicks.
The team finished even in turnovers, with one giveaway and one takeaway. Stefanski wants to keep winning that margin and playing complementary football.

title: Jesse Minter Optimistic About Ravens' Health Entering Week 3
headline: Ronnie Stanley (street clothes) is the one real health question for Sunday's Brazil game vs. Dallas; Minter is optimistic on others, and says Lamar Jackson's lower rushing is partly circumstantial and partly read-based.
summary: Minter opened by thanking the NFL, Botafogo and the Ravens' operations staff for the trip to Rio, saying the team arrived this morning and had a productive first practice. He said the group has the right leaders and has moved past the home loss to the Saints, with the focus on a good Cowboys team. On injuries, he was non-committal on Ronnie Stanley, who was in street clothes, saying his status could go all the way up to game day or be decided soon, and that he would revisit it after returning. He sounded upbeat about the other injured players, saying they have a real chance to help in the game. On Lamar Jackson's declining rushing totals, he called it a bit of both: designed quarterback runs are being called but the defense's read has often told Lamar to hand off. He admitted the offense has been hurt by penalties (12 offensive fouls through two games, many pre-snap), calling it a major emphasis, and said the unit could be among the league's best if it stops hurting itself. He described the team's identity as still developing, with good stretches in all three phases but inconsistency. He also said he expects a loud, road-like atmosphere for both teams, and the field at Maracana is not seen as an advantage for either side.

title: Joe Brady Gives Injury Updates Ahead Of Week 3 Vs The Chargers And More
headline: DJ Moore and Keon Coleman are both questionable for Sunday night vs. the Chargers, with Brady holding the decision until game time; Ty Johnson is good to go and Josh Palmer could see a bigger role.
summary: Brady said Jordan Hancock and T.J. Sanders will be out, while DJ Moore, Keon Coleman and Ed Oliver (confirmed as questionable after a follow-up question) are questionable. He said he will give the questionable players until game time because he trusts them to know where they are in the process. He has multiple contingency plans for the receiver room if Moore or Coleman can't go, and said whoever is out there will have his full trust. Brady praised Josh Palmer's detailed route running and his rapport with Josh Allen, and said he sees Palmer continuing to progress. Moore sat out Thursday's practice and Brady called it a decision aimed at helping him get to the game, saying there is a chance he can play Sunday. Ty Johnson will be good to go Sunday night after taking time to get back, and Brady said he brings a dimension that forces defenses to defend differently. Rookie Skyler Bell is still getting reps with the ones and with Allen in practice, and is learning from Khalil Shakir and Moore. Brady stressed that players need to be ready on short notice, as the team learned last week, and said the offense is simple enough this early in the season to put people in.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference : September 25th, 2026
headline: Deshaun Watson is the starter and had his best week of practice; two unnamed Browns players are questionable and the coach says the run game must improve.
summary: Monken opened by praising Nick Chubb, who spoke to the team at practice about preparation and enjoying the moment. Monken said Chubb is one of the most respected players he has been around. He said two players are questionable, went through practice, and will do extra work afterward. He is hopeful both can play but gave no names or details on how they were hurt. He said Mason Graham played better in Week 2, but he credited the whole team and staff for improving and winning more one-on-ones. On Deshaun Watson, he said this was Watson's best week of practice, that his confidence should be at an all-time high, and that Watson has become the starter and is just scratching the surface. Facing Carolina, he downplayed the absence of linebacker Devin Lloyd, saying he didn't know about it and that teams must be ready with the next man up. He also stressed staying humble in a week-to-week league after a Week 1 blowout and a Week 2 win. On the offense, he said that with or without Chubb's visit, the team has to run the ball better.

On injuries, he said the only players left behind were P.J. Locke and LT Overton, and everyone else who traveled is good to go. Today's practice was about an hour of light work to knock off the rust after the flight, with walkthroughs on Saturday and a re-hit of first and second down work from Tuesday. He acknowledged the Ravens' challenge, citing the speed of Derrick Henry and Lamar Jackson, and said any defensive mistake opens a gap they can punish. He leaned on veteran Markquese Bell to step in, said Shavon Revel needs to play, and praised rookie Jaishawn Barham's work as the green-dot signal caller last week, adding that Dee Winters is improving. He also admitted the offense is bad under center right now, even though the staff believes in the approach because it disguises tendencies. He closed with the team's focus on routine, faith, and bonding.

title: Matt LaFleur: 'We’ve got to find solutions'
headline: Packers' offense is in crisis after a humbling Thursday loss to Atlanta: just nine rushes on 50+ dropbacks, RB1 is wide open ('everybody is in competition'), and Jordan Love is taking heavy punishment behind a struggling line.
